stories.topic: Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
stories.text: Ukraine launches a large-scale drone attack across western Russia, striking the Perm refinery in Perm Krai and Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov Oblast.
Turkish intelligence reports that the Kurdistan Workers' Party withdraws from 14 additional bases in northern Iraq as part of an ongoing disarmament process aimed at ending its conflict with Turkey.
At least 15 people are injured and 28 houses and shops are vandalised during clashes between rival Bangladesh Nationalist Party factions in Shailkupa Upazila, Jhenaidah District, Bangladesh.

At least 20 people are injured, five seriously, and several shops are vandalised as rival factions of the banned Awami League clash and detonate four crude bombs in Gopalganj Sadar Upazila, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh.

stories.topic: Jensen Huang scandal, Chinese intelligence activity abroad
stories.text: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer less than two weeks after he resigned following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China.
Seven people are killed and two others are injured after a truck loaded with stones overturns onto a minitruck in Punjab, Pakistan.
A 58-year-old student dies at Sapienza University in Rome, Italy, while being on a hunger strike protesting the fact that he had not been assigned a place to stay.

stories.topic: Myanmar–United Kingdom relations, Rohingya genocide case
stories.text: The United Kingdom's foreign secretary Ed Miliband announces sanctions against five military leaders of Myanmar, while also granting recognition of the Rohingya genocide.
Tajikistan formally begins the process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court.

The Supreme Court of Spain grants amnesty to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who is currently in self-imposed exile in Belgium, thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the October 2017 declaration of independence to a definitive close.
Hundreds of schools across Denmark and Germany receive bomb threats via email, with police ordering the schools to continue operations as normal.
Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi receives 74 lashes for performing at a music concert without a hijab.

stories.topic: Censorship in Bangladesh, Human rights in Bangladesh
stories.text: Amnesty International urges Bangladesh to withdraw its draft Cyber Protection (Amendment) Act, 2026, warning that vague provisions allow authorities to censor online content, impose up to five-year imprisonment for speech, arbitrarily arrest critics, and grant officials immunity for human rights abuses.

stories.topic: 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids
stories.text: In association football, FIFA confirms Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales will jointly host the 2035 tournament.
